checks.name: visibility targets (event/env, base-ref recovery, deepening)
reads: env GITHUB_EVENT_NAME, GITHUB_EVENT_PATH, GITHUB_BASE_REF
event JSON payload (pull_request.head.sha, pull_request.base.ref)
git refs HEAD / refs/remotes/origin/<base ref>
NETWORK: git fetch origin (+refs/heads/<ref>:refs/remotes/origin/<ref>, --unshallow/--deepen; and fetch of each target sha) only when shallow or base ref unresolved
checks.protects: That every derivation is evaluated over the A.37 visibility union (real PR head + live origin/<base>), never pull_request.base.sha, a local branch or the synthetic merge; on non-pull_request events the single target is HEAD.
checks.reason: The visibility union exists only to make the A.37 landing-merge (L) derivation robust for long-lived execution PRs; any surviving historical check can use plain HEAD. Note: every git derivation below consumes these targets, so retiring it requires rebinding survivors to HEAD.
checks.v3_pr_can_fail: yes, environment-only: on a pull_request run it fails closed if the event payload is missing/unparsable, or origin/<base> cannot be resolved (shallow/single-branch checkout and fetch fails). Content of a V3 round cannot trigger it. The Mathlib bridge job checks out with fetch-depth: 0 (verify.yml:74), so it passes in the normal case.

checks.name: store presence and stray files
reads: working tree: listing of verification/certificates/*.json (non-.json and subdirectories ignored)
checks.protects: The certificate store exists and its root holds only STEM-named certificate JSON plus live-policy.json and legacy-v1-owned.json.
checks.reason: Cheap integrity of the directory holding the immutable legacy records; a stray/renamed certificate is a damaged record.
checks.v3_pr_can_fail: no: fires only if the PR removes verification/certificates or adds a non-stem .json at its root.

checks.name: certificate schema
reads: working tree: verification/certificates/<STEM>.json (52 files)
checks.protects: Each certificate is well-formed JSON of the frozen oi-round-certificate schema (protocol 1|2, origin, shape, topology fields per shape, evidence/contribution/dependency lists, translation block iff translated-v1).
checks.reason: The parser of the 52 frozen records; evidence resolution depends on it. Topology/translation sub-rules are V2-protocol shape but cost nothing on frozen data. translation.migration_snapshot is hex-checked only, never compared to git.
checks.v3_pr_can_fail: no: only if a certificate file is edited.

checks.name: attestation-record schema
reads: working tree: verification/certificates/attestations/<STEM>.json (36 files)
checks.protects: Each attestation record is well-formed: landed rows carry sealed_head/tree/landing, base-only rows forbid them; translated rows carry migration_snapshot and no ci; native/bootstrap rows carry ci{exact_e,exact_l,main_push}.
checks.reason: Parser of frozen records. The ci block (A.37 exact-head CI attestation) and migration_snapshot are schema-checked only; no check compares them with GitHub or git.
checks.v3_pr_can_fail: no: only if an attestation file is edited.

checks.name: corpus provenance / ledger pairing
reads: in-memory store (certificates + attestation filenames)
checks.protects: At most one bootstrap-v1 certificate; content-only rounds have no row; every translated non-content-only certificate has a row; no row lacks a certificate.
checks.reason: Detects deletion of a legacy attestation record (ledger-row-removed vector) or an orphan row. second-bootstrap is V2 provenance and can only fire if a certificate is added.
checks.v3_pr_can_fail: no: only if certificates/rows are added or removed.

checks.name: row-to-certificate binding (incl. certificate blob pin)
reads: working tree certificate blob (translated-v1: 35 rows)
git object: verification/certificates/<STEM>.json at the recorded sealed_head (non-translated landed rows: CV1 only)
checks.protects: Row and certificate agree on protocol/origin/base, and the row's certificate hash equals the certificate: for translated rows the CURRENT file blob (this is what makes the 35 row-backed translated certificates immutable), for CV1 the blob at its sealed head.
checks.reason: The only mechanism pinning the 35 row-backed translated certificate files. Gaps: the 16 content-only certificates and CV1's current file are not blob-pinned by anything in V2.
checks.v3_pr_can_fail: no: only if a certificate or row is edited.

checks.name: legacy-v1-owned partition
reads: working tree: verification/certificates/legacy-v1-owned.json (1 entry: PRA)
checks.protects: The V1/V2 ownership partition: at most one round (PRA) is certified by the prior protocol and it has no V2 certificate/row.
checks.reason: Encodes which protocol (V1 vs V2) decides a round's validity -- superseded once V3 is the authority; it makes no validity claim about PRA itself.
checks.v3_pr_can_fail: no (file-presence/schema only; a V3 round does not touch it).

checks.name: legacy-owned preregistration blob pin and base existence
reads: working tree: verification/programmes/oi-qm/track-b/act-29-product-admission/preregistration.md (blob 5451a52d...)
git object db: commit 0bedff07... exists
checks.protects: PRA's frozen preregistration is unchanged in the tree and its recorded base commit exists.
checks.reason: Immutability of a landed round's frozen preregistration; the base-existence half is an object-existence check only (rebind-able).
checks.v3_pr_can_fail: no: only if PRA's preregistration is edited/moved or the clone lacks that commit.

checks.name: B derivation: control-plane blob introduction -> recorded merge -> base
reads: git topology: git log --first-parent --find-object=<blob> <target> for each of the 42 control-plane blobs over each visibility target
git trees: ls-tree -r at every hit and its first parent
checks.protects: For each of the 36 non-content-only certificates, each frozen control-plane artifact entered first-parent history at exactly one commit, equal to the recorded merge, and the last execution-affecting one is the recorded mandated base B (A.37 D/B chronology).
checks.reason: Pure A.37 control-plane->base chronology. The artifact-integrity half is redundant: all 42 control-plane blobs are also pinned as the same certificate's evidence (V2-EVID) in the current tree.
checks.v3_pr_can_fail: conditionally yes: on a pull_request run the union of first-parent walks is used; if the PR branch absorbed main through a merge whose FIRST parent is the branch (GitHub "Update branch") after one of the 42 control-plane merges, that merge is a second introducing commit -> base:multiple-candidates (reproduced in a scratch repo with git 2.43). A conforming V3 round (D after all 42 merges; reconciliation first parent = later base per A.39) cannot hit it. Also base:git on git failure.

checks.name: landed-row commits exist
reads: git object db: base, sealed_head, landing commits of the 30 landed rows
checks.protects: The commits a landed record names are present in the repository.
checks.reason: As "the recorded commits of a historical record resolve" it is object-level record integrity; under V2 it is the precondition of the E/L chronology.
checks.v3_pr_can_fail: no, except a clone missing those objects.

checks.name: E derivation and strong ancestry
reads: git topology: parents of recorded landing; merge-base --is-ancestor; rev-list <sealed> ^<base> and per-commit ancestry
checks.protects: The recorded sealed head is the unique non-first parent of the recorded landing that descends strongly from base (no pre-freeze side history), i.e. the A.37 sealed-execution chronology.
checks.reason: A.37 E/L/base chronology. Caveat: over immutable commits it is deterministic, so in practice it can only fire if a row's base/sealed_head/landing field is edited -- attestation rows have NO blob pin anywhere in V2, so retiring V2-TOPO-* removes their only edit protection unless replaced by a row blob pin.
checks.v3_pr_can_fail: no (deterministic over fixed commits; only a row edit or missing objects).

checks.name: tree(sealed_head) equals recorded tree
reads: git object: tree of recorded sealed_head (subject=certified; current-tree subject only in corpus vectors)
checks.protects: The recorded tree is exactly the content of the certified sealed head.
checks.reason: Useful as record integrity (the recorded tree identifies what was certified), not as a validity verdict.
checks.v3_pr_can_fail: no (deterministic; only a row edit).

checks.name: L derivation: unique landing over the visibility union
reads: git topology: git log --format="%H %P" over full history of each visibility target
checks.protects: Exactly one merge visible from the targets carries the sealed head as a non-first parent, and it equals the recorded landing (A.37 landing visibility / no rewritten landing).
checks.reason: A.37 landing choreography over the PR-head/base-tip visibility union.
checks.v3_pr_can_fail: practically no: requires a new merge with a legacy sealed head as non-first parent (V3 reconciliation merges take E_v3 or a receipt commit) or git failure; zero-candidates impossible while the landing is on main.

checks.name: base-only row base reachable
reads: git object db and ancestry of the 6 base-only rows' base against the visibility targets
checks.protects: A base-only record's base exists and is an ancestor of some visibility target.
checks.reason: As "the recorded base is in main's history" it is record integrity; its visibility-target framing is V2.
checks.v3_pr_can_fail: no (bases are already on main).

checks.name: dependency closure (fixpoint)
reads: in-memory certificates (15 dependency edges over 52 certificates)
checks.protects: Every declared dependency names an existing certificate of no later protocol, and a failing dependency fails its dependents.
checks.reason: Internal consistency of the frozen record graph; its failure propagation carries whatever checks survive. protocol-order is a V2 rule that cannot fire on the frozen corpus (all protocol 1).
checks.v3_pr_can_fail: no: only through a certificate edit or a propagated failure.

checks.name: evidence blob pins (universal live rule)
reads: working tree: the 157 evidence paths of certificates whose verdict is PASS (90 under verification/programmes, 26 infrastructure, 8 audits, 33 verification/seals/<STEM>.json)
checks.protects: Every evidence file of every accepted legacy round (preregistrations incl. all 42 control-plane artifacts, results, census/data, 33 seal records) is present at its path with its certified blob.
checks.reason: The core integrity property of already-landed records. Note it is gated on verdict==PASS (line 858): a certificate failing any other check has its evidence skipped (the run still fails). This is the only way V2 reads verification/seals (as pinned blobs; no seal semantics). Contributions (202 paths) are never pinned.
checks.v3_pr_can_fail: no, unless the PR edits, moves or deletes one of the 157 pinned files (e.g. a legacy result.md, preregistration or verification/seals/*.json).

checks.name: relocation ledger
reads: working tree: verification/certificates/relocations/*.json (directory absent: 0 records)
working tree existence of relocation source paths
checks.protects: An evidence file may move only via a contiguous, blob-preserving, non-forking relocation record, after which the old path must be gone.
checks.reason: The sanctioned way to move a historical evidence file without breaking its pin; vacuous today (no records).
checks.v3_pr_can_fail: no (no relocation records exist; only if the PR adds one).

checks.name: live policy
reads: working tree: verification/certificates/live-policy.json (count 0, policies [])
working tree paths named by clause predicates (none)
checks.protects: Round-owned live tree predicates (blob-pinned, path-absent, file-contains, file-lacks) hold on the current tree; the file must exist with protocol 2 and exact count.
checks.reason: A V2 mechanism for round-owned live rules with zero clauses; today only its file-presence/schema can fail. (Rebind only if an owner wants a generic tree-predicate list.)
checks.v3_pr_can_fail: no (0 clauses; only if the file is removed/edited).

checks.name: conformance corpus executed as an exact set
reads: working tree: verification/certificates/conformance/v2/*.json (89 vectors + expected.json)
writes/reads temp dirs via tempfile.mkdtemp (87 synthetic repos; 2 vacuity vectors build none; 6 subject:current-tree vectors evaluate twice)
spawns git with os.environ copy; synthetic GITHUB_EVENT_* for 10 pull_request vectors
checks.protects: The verifier implementation reproduces the expected verdict/reason on every fixture and executes exactly the corpus (no dropped/substituted vectors).
checks.reason: Self-test of whatever checks survive; vectors of retired families (ambiguity 6, visibility 8, topology 6, historical-subject 6, legacy-owned 5, live-policy 9, most provenance) must retire with them, and exact-set vacuity keeps the rest honest.
checks.v3_pr_can_fail: no from content; yes from environment (git missing/incompatible, unwritable temp dir -> ERROR mismatch).

checks.name: uncaught exception path
reads: n/a
checks.protects: Not a designed check: an unexpected exception (e.g. OSError reading a pinned file that isfile() admitted) aborts with a non-zero exit in either mode.
checks.reason: Fail-closed default; not a policy. Listed for exhaustiveness (ambiguous whether to count as a check).
checks.v3_pr_can_fail: only on I/O faults.

readers.gating: job not a required check per its own comment

readers.what: Mathlib bridge job runs tools/release_gate.py, hence the authoritative step (fetch-depth: 0 at :74)

ATTESTATION_DIR = verification/certificates/attestations/; project() reads rows at a subject via git ls-tree; used only by --project (1461-1464) and --mode shadow (1465-1478, invoked verify.yml:310); never by --receipts
checks the CV1 base had no certificates dir / verifier (git rev-parse at _CV1_B)
_cv1_run_verifier: runs certificate_verifier.py --mode shadow --root <root> as subprocess and parses CERT/ROW/VECTOR/LEGACY-V1-OWNED/summary lines; checks verifier-ran, verifier-shadow-ok
bridge simulation: builds synthetic repos with verification/certificates/{ZZ.json,attestations/ZZ.json,legacy-v1-owned.json} and runs verifier --no-corpus

_cv1_store parses certificates + attestations; provenance-one-bootstrap-and-it-is-cv1, fifty-one translated, thirty-five translated rows; legacy-owned-exactly-pra; live-policy-zero-clauses; no-relocation-record
reads verify.yml text (workflow-job-in-shadow: shadow present, authoritative absent) and release_gate.py text (release-gate-authoritative-step)
CV1 additive-diff root list; rep6b PRA LEGACY-V1-OWNED report over _CV1_CERT_OBJS
recorded historical V2 shadow summary lines (data, not an invocation)
lists tools/certificate_verifier.py as a CV1 contribution (not blob-pinned)

counts.corpus_execution: run_corpus lists conformance/v2/*.json, requires each vector id == filename and vector.expect == expected.json[id]; each non-vacuity vector builds a fresh git repo in a tempfile.mkdtemp dir with commit-tree (exact parent order, placeholder substitution), synthesizes GITHUB_EVENT_* (pull_request payload file under .git) and calls evaluate() on it; verdict/reason compared to expected (prefix match); finally exact_set(executed, sorted(expected)) must hold. Serial, ~27s total.

run_self_test.note: self_test 1073-1147: pure schema/exact_set/legacy/policy fixtures plus one synthetic repo evaluate (push); no repository read

notes: UNATTESTED verdict (874-876) produces no failure code; it is report-only.
Non-failing inputs: contributions (schema only), row ci run ids/conclusions and head_shas (hex-only), migration_snapshot (hex-only) are never checked against git or GitHub.

Attestation rows are not blob-pinned by V2; their only protection is re-derivation by V2-ROW-CERT/V2-TOPO-*/V2-BASEONLY. The 16 content-only certificates and the current CV1.json are not blob-pinned either (schema + evidence + dependencies only).
Evidence resolution runs only over certificates with verdict PASS (line 858).
The tool never reads verification/receipts/ and never interprets verification/seals/ records; it only blob-pins 33 of them as evidence.
Network: only git fetch from origin in Git.recover/Git.deepen, triggered only by a shallow checkout or an unresolved origin/<base ref> on pull_request events.

V2-BASE multiple-candidates on a branch that absorbed main via a first-parent-branch merge was confirmed with a scratch repo (git 2.43): --first-parent --find-object reports the absorbing merge as introducing the blob.
